Require authorization on certificates referenced via replaces/replacements

The replaces/replacements field on certificate create, upload, and edit
requests let an authenticated caller reference an arbitrary certificate
by ID without any ownership or role check, silencing its expiration
notifications and retargeting its rotation. Enforce the same
CertificatePermission check used for direct revoke/edit on every
certificate named in replaces before the request is processed.

All authenticated endpoints require a short-lived access token in the `Authorization` header:
```bash
Authorization: Bearer <your-access-token>
```

The **refresh token** is stored server-side as an `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Strict` cookie
set by `/auth/login` and `/auth/register`. To refresh the access token, `POST /api/v1/auth/refresh`
with that cookie attached (browsers do this automatically; from `curl`, use `-b/-c` cookie jars).
The refresh endpoint does **not** accept a refresh token in the request body or `Authorization`
header — it reads exclusively from the cookie.

## 📡 API Endpoints

### Authentication
- `POST /api/v1/auth/register` - Register new user (sets refresh cookie)
- `POST /api/v1/auth/login` - Login user (sets refresh cookie)
- `POST /api/v1/auth/refresh` - Refresh access token (reads refresh cookie; no body required)
- `POST /api/v1/auth/logout` - Clear the refresh cookie

### Workouts
- `GET /api/v1/exercises` - Get all exercises
- `GET /api/v1/exercises/search?muscleGroup=&equipmentType=` - Search exercises with filters
- `POST /api/v1/workouts` - Start new workout (body: `date` required)
- `POST /api/v1/workouts/{id}/sets` - Log a set
- `PUT /api/v1/workouts/{id}/finish` - Finish workout
- `GET /api/v1/workouts/active` - Get in-progress workout (204 if none)
- `GET /api/v1/workouts/history?startDate=&endDate=` - Get workout history (both dates required, ISO YYYY-MM-DD)
- `GET /api/v1/workouts/{id}` - Get workout details

- [x] Frontend: exercise library, workout session, set logging, history, workout detail modal
- [x] Database migrations V3 (exercises), V4 (workouts), V5 (workout_sets)

Changelog
=========

1.9.3 - `unreleased`
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
- Fixed arbitrary certificate revocation at the CA (`GHSA-pxmc-2ffp-8j67`_). Certificate identity was tracked
  only by Lemur's internal database row, not by the actual CA-side certificate. Any authenticated user could
  upload a duplicate record for a certificate they didn't own (matching an existing ``authority_id`` and
  ``serial``) and then revoke it via ``PUT /api/1/certificates/<id>/revoke``, causing the CA to revoke the
  real certificate belonging to another user. ``POST /api/1/certificates/upload`` now requires
  ``AuthorityPermission`` on the specified authority, and rejects uploads whose ``(authority_id, serial)``
  pair already matches an existing certificate with a ``409`` response. ``PUT /api/1/certificates/<id>/revoke``
  now also checks authorization and endpoint attachment against every certificate row sharing
  ``(authority_id, serial)`` with the one being revoked, not just the row named in the request, closing the
  gap for any duplicate rows that already exist.

STOMP server process client frames that would not send initially a connect frame

A Vert.x STOMP server processes client STOMP frames without checking that the client send an initial CONNECT frame replied with a successful CONNECTED frame. The client can subscribe to a destination or publish message without prior authentication. Any Vert.x STOMP server configured with an authentication handler is impacted.

fix: real live API-key verification, working window drag, minimize button

Real bugs found while testing the native build:
- src-tauri/capabilities/ didn't exist, so Tauri v2's ACL granted almost no
  permissions by default — including core:window:allow-start-dragging, which
  is why dragging the header did nothing. Added the standard default.json.
- The header had no minimize control; the hide_window Rust command already
  existed but was never wired to any UI.
- Percentages were still placeholder-looking (85/92/78/64) even though
  labeled "estimated" — entering a real key had no visible effect since
  local-session detection already showed the same static numbers.

Replaced format-only key validation with a real live check: a new
verify_api_key Rust command (via reqwest, avoids browser CORS entirely)
makes one lightweight authenticated request to the provider and reports
whether the key actually works, plus any real rate-limit numbers the
response includes. A quota percentage is now shown ONLY when a provider's
response actually contained a rate-limit header (hasQuotaData) — local
session detection and providers without quota headers show connection
status with no invented number. Rejected keys now surface the real reason
(e.g. "Provider rejected this key (HTTP 401)") instead of silently doing
nothing.

Security bug fixes
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

-   When a :class:`~scrapy.http.Request` object with cookies defined gets a
    redirect response causing a new :class:`~scrapy.http.Request` object to be
    scheduled, the cookies defined in the original
    :class:`~scrapy.http.Request` object are no longer copied into the new
    :class:`~scrapy.http.Request` object.

    If you manually set the ``Cookie`` header on a
    :class:`~scrapy.http.Request` object and the domain name of the redirect
    URL is not an exact match for the domain of the URL of the original
    :class:`~scrapy.http.Request` object, your ``Cookie`` header is now dropped
    from the new :class:`~scrapy.http.Request` object.

    The old behavior could be exploited by an attacker to gain access to your
    cookies. Please, see the `cjvr-mfj7-j4j8 security advisory`_ for more
    information.

              your cookies. See the documentation of the

        """
        Allow the backend to clean the username, if the backend defines a
        clean_username method.

        backend_str = request.session[auth.BACKEND_SESSION_KEY]
        backend = auth.load_backend(backend_str)
        try:

class APIKeyQuery(APIKeyBase):
    """
    API key authentication using a query parameter.

    This defines the name of the query parameter that should be provided in the request
    with the API key and integrates that into the OpenAPI documentation. It extracts
    the key value sent in the query parameter automatically and provides it as the
    dependency result. But it doesn't define how to send that API key to the client.

    ## Usage

    Create an instance object and use that object as the dependency in `Depends()`.

    The dependency result will be a string containing the key value.

    ## Example

    ```python
    from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI
    from fastapi.security import APIKeyQuery

    app = FastAPI()

    query_scheme = APIKeyQuery(name="api_key")

    @app.get("/items/")
    async def read_items(api_key: str = Depends(query_scheme)):
        return {"api_key": api_key}
    ```
    """

4.  Register URLs: `path('mfa/', include('mfa.urls', namespace='mfa')`
5.  The included templates are just examples, so you should [replace them](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/stable/howto/overriding-templates/) with your own

def custom_login(self, request, extra_context=None):
    next_url = (
        request.GET.get(REDIRECT_FIELD_NAME)
        or request.POST.get(REDIRECT_FIELD_NAME)

feat(web): add the attended web-release plan/apply chain, interlocked against the legacy CD carrier (TIN-3816) (#111)

* fix(web): bind web image admission to the stack under validation (TIN-3816)

scripts/validate-web-stack.sh admitted its image with a flat repository
test that was independent of the stack being validated, so the guard
described "some GFTB web image" rather than "this stack's image". The
admitted repository is now looked up from the Deployment's own target
namespace:

  greatfallstoolbus-org-production -> greatfallstoolbus-org
                                   -> ghcr.io/great-falls-tool-bus/greatfallstoolbus.org

A namespace with no table entry fails closed, the Deployment's name must
match the workload the namespace admits, and every per-container
assertion binds to that name through a jq --arg rather than a literal, so
a stack cannot rename its container out from under the probe and
hardening checks.

The digest test is also tightened from a `@sha256:*` glob to a full
64-lowercase-hex match. Verified rejections against a scratch copy of the
stack (each rc=1):

  ghcr.io/great-falls-tool-bus/gftb-site@sha256:<64 zeros>   other repository
  ghcr.io/great-falls-tool-bus/greatfallstoolbus.org:latest  tag reference
  ghcr.io/elsewhere/greatfallstoolbus.org@sha256:<64 hex>    foreign owner
  ...greatfallstoolbus.org@sha256:<63 hex>                   truncated digest
  ...greatfallstoolbus.org@sha256:<64 UPPER hex>             uppercase digest
  namespace rewritten to gftb-site-production                unknown stack

The gftb-site static-origin candidate is admitted on a different axis and
is never committed to a manifest: it arrives as WEB_APPLY_IMAGE and is
held to its own exact digest shape by _web-release-candidate-inputs.

WEB_RELEASE_VALIDATION_SCRIPT_SHA256 is re-pinned to the new bytes so the
PR #109 receipt keeps covering this script.

* feat(web): add the attended web-release plan/apply chain (TIN-3816)

PR #109 landed the proof-only half of the gftb-site release
(_web-release-candidate-inputs, web-release-candidate-proof,
web-release-render, web-release-pinned-running-proof,
web-release-served-proof) and left the mutating half to a separately
reviewed exact-render/apply/rollback contract. This is that half, in the
same recipe family and on the same input contract.

  web-release-plan            renders ONCE through web-release-render and
                              records the exact bytes, their SHA-256, the
                              selected image + source SHA, and the infra
                              carrier commit under .k8s-plans/ (0700,
                              artifacts 0600, gitignored)
  _web-release-plan-preflight re-renders and refuses unless the render is
                              byte-identical and the inputs and carrier
                              are unchanged
  web-release-server-dry-run  server-side dry-run of the recorded bytes
  web-release-apply           _reviewed-clean-main + GFTB_APPLY_CONFIRM +
                              kubeconfig custody + plan preflight, then
                              dry-run, apply the recorded bytes, prune the
                              two legacy egress policies the render omits
                              (apply does not prune omissions), roll out

There is exactly ONE renderer: web-release-render. Nothing in the chain
resolves an image, runs `kubectl set image`, or patches replicas -- the
render already bakes ${WEB_APPLY_IMAGE} and replicas: 2 into the bytes,
so the live pod template can only be a render of reviewed inputs. The
apply identity is the existing WEB_APPLY_KUBECONFIG (no new credential),
now held to the ARC custody bar: operator-owned, mode 0600, outside every
repository tree, ambient KUBECONFIG refused.

Guard contract (was: dependencies only; the reviewer showed nine body
mutations all produced zero findings):

- every recipe joins WEB_RELEASE_RECIPE_DEPENDENCIES *and*
  WEB_RELEASE_CRITICAL_RECIPE_DIGESTS, so bodies are digest-pinned the
  same way ARC pins its critical recipes; header shape, recipe
  attributes, alias collisions, and the operator-local closure come with
  that family for free
- WEB_RELEASE_STACK_GLOBAL_ASSIGNMENTS pins web_stack_dir/web_stack_ns,
  so redirecting the rendered/applied stack is a finding
- IMPERATIVE_PIN now scans the WHOLE Justfile (every recipe body plus
  every executable line outside a recipe) instead of three named
  recipes, with exactly one allowlisted legacy carrier
  (web-stack-apply); the allowlist itself fails closed if that recipe is
  renamed or removed

mutations (apply detached from the recorded plan, preflight without the
re-render proof, preflight without the carrier binding, kubeconfig
custody without the mode check, a second renderer in the plan), two
stack-global redirections, four imperative-pin fixtures including a
brand-new unlisted `web-release-hotfix` recipe, and a stale allowlist.

site repo on every push to main -- runs `just web-stack-apply`, which would
re-pin the adapter-node digest over the promoted static origin and recreate the
two legacy egress NetworkPolicies web-release-apply deletes. The next green push

`web-stack-apply` now takes `_web-stack-promotion-interlock` as its FIRST
dependency. The interlock reads the LIVE Deployment image and refuses when it
already carries a ghcr.io/great-falls-tool-bus/gftb-site reference, before the
dry-run and before any mutation. web-stack-apply stays the single allowlisted

verb the chain needs before it touches anything: get/list/watch/create/update/
patch on deployments.apps, get/create/update/patch on services and
networkpolicies, and delete on networkpolicies. `apply --dry-run=server` does not
authorize the delete, so without this a green dry-run could be followed by a
successful apply and a denied prune -- a half-done promotion running the new
image with allow-egress-dns still permitting egress.

feat(permissions): add Field::SELF_REQUIRES, a relation-scoped OR alternative to the target read gate

When an edge/join re-projects a field through its own AQL::FIELDS,
authorizeTargetFields() (the T6 guard) re-applies the target model's
Field::REQUIRES so a masked field cannot be re-exposed through the
relation. That inheritance was absolute — a relation could never declare
that, in its own context, another permission suffices.

Field::SELF_REQUIRES lifts exactly that, and only that: a field refused
by the target model is kept when it declares SELF_REQUIRES and the
authorizer grants at least one of its subjects (logical OR). It is read
only by authorizeTargetFields(); first-level model reads never pass
through that helper, so the T6 guard stays intact everywhere else.

Affirmative grant only: the subjects are normalized to a non-empty list
of strings before the check, so an empty/malformed SELF_REQUIRES cannot
borrow isAuthorized()'s "no subject -> allowed" fail-open and silently
re-open the hole T6 closes. Backward compatible: with no SELF_REQUIRES
the behaviour is byte-for-byte the former gate; fail-open unchanged.

notification.service.url was hardcoded to http://localhost:8087 in the dev
profile - nothing listens there. notification-service's real dev port is
8059. Every OTP send hit connection-refused, was caught by
sendOtpInternalJwt's outer try/catch, and logged (not surfaced) as a

delivery failure (already documented in its own docstring) - surfacing it
would leak whether a given identifier has an account, since it's also

fix(ui): show all action chips, authenticate at dispatch from declared SoT (#2151)

Product rule (user, 2026-08-19): "we show all actions and then we
authenticate when the UC requires it, and we have SOT."

The whole action region sat behind `{isLoggedIn && renderActionGroups()}`
inside an `isLoggedIn ? … : …` ternary, so a guest saw a login prompt
INSTEAD of the action surface. That broke the rule twice: it removed the
demo's discovery story, and it invented a second source of truth (a bare
isLoggedIn at a render site) alongside the uc.auth SoT the rest of the
app gates on.

- Discovery ungated: renderActionGroups() renders for everyone, moved
  above the ternary. The guest branch keeps its own "get started" login
  chips — additive to the actions, not a substitute for them.
- Auth moved to DISPATCH: handleChipActivate reads the chip's declared
  level and, when the viewer doesn't meet it, offers sign-in
  (showLoginPromptAction — the same shape handleDemoStepSelect uses for
  use-case tiles) instead of dispatching.
- Declared SoT for chips: chips are not use cases and carry no server
  uc.auth, so PUBLIC_CHIP_IDS / ADMIN_CHIP_IDS / chipAuthLevel() live in
  agentActions.js — one place, not a condition invented per call site.

FAIL-CLOSED by construction: anything undeclared needs a session, and a
blank/missing id resolves to 'user', never 'public'. Ungating the render
WITHOUT this dispatch gate would have handed guests chips that dispatch
straight to the BFF and fail as a 401 round-trip — the opposite of the
rule — which is why both halves ship together.

mcp_tools is public deliberately: its endpoint carries no auth
middleware and answers 200 anonymously (recorded on the route as
INTENTIONALLY UNAUTHENTICATED). It sits in the `admin` GROUP for menu
placement only — UI grouping is not an authorization boundary.

Two pre-existing tests asserted the OPPOSITE contract ("does not render
action items when user is null"); both were rewritten to pin the new
rule, including a click-through proving a guest gets the sign-in offer
rather than a dispatch. REGRESSION_PLAN §4 entry added (§1 UI surface).

Strict meta channel recognition in server

This addresses a security vulnerability affecting user-added extensions
that implement access control for channels. These extensions typically
work by checking incoming messages whose channel is `/meta/subscribe`
and then performing some authentication routine before allowing the
message through.

However, the Server parses channels in a way that means any channel
namespaced under `/meta/subscribe` will also work as a subscription
request. For example if the client sends a message to the channel
`/meta/subscribe/x`, that will bypass most authentication extensions but
will still be interpreted by the server as a subscription request, and
the client will be subscribed to the requested channel. The client has
thus bypassed the user's access control policy.

Here we prevent this by using a strict equality check; only messages
whose channel is exactly `/meta/subscribe` will be interpreted as
subscription requests. The same pattern is applied to all other meta
channels.

explanation:
Fix real vulnerabilities found in a dedicated security audit

Three parallel audits (auth/authz, injection/input-handling, secrets/
infrastructure) covering the whole app, adversarial lens. Fixes:

CRITICAL
- MFA was completely bypassable: the 5-minute "mfa_pending" challenge
  token issued by /auth/login (before a TOTP/backup code is ever
  checked) decoded and passed get_current_user()'s checks exactly like
  a real session token -- anyone with just a password (the one thing
  MFA exists to add a second factor against) could call any
  authenticated endpoint directly with it, no code required, for the
  full 5-minute window. Now explicitly rejected, same pattern as the
  existing "purpose" claim check.

HIGH
- Twilio webhook signature verification failed OPEN (skipped, request
  allowed through) when TWILIO_TOKEN/PUBLIC_BASE_URL were unset --
  now fails closed (503), matching the pattern already used correctly
  for CRON_SECRET/EMAIL_WORKER_SECRET.
- SECRET_KEY/JWT_SECRET ship with hardcoded, publicly-known placeholder
  defaults with no code-level guard against running with them in
  production (only Render's generateValue: true prevented this on the
  documented deploy path). App now refuses to boot with DEBUG=false if
  either is still its literal default.

MODERATE
- Three IDOR gaps: POST /communications/send's maintenance_update
  template, POST /maintenance/'s unit_id/tenant_id, and POST
  /accounting/expenses' vendor_id all accepted a foreign org's UUID
  with no ownership check, leaking that resource's name/title/status
  back in the response. All now validated against the caller's org.
- Unescaped HTML injection in three outreach-email templates
  (services/lead_service.py) -- lead fields (scraped from public,
  attacker-editable Google Business Profile data, or typed into
  POST /leads with no sanitization) were interpolated into HTML emails
  with no output encoding. Now html.escape()'d for the HTML body
  specifically (plain-text body unaffected).
- SSRF in the lead-scraper's email-discovery fetch
  (workers/tasks/lead_scraping.py) -- a Places listing's self-reported
  website URL was fetched with no scheme/private-IP allowlist and
  followed redirects blindly, so a listing pointed at an internal
  address or a cloud metadata endpoint would have the server fetch it.
  Added an SSRF guard checked on the initial URL and re-checked on
  every redirect hop.
- FastAPI backend sent no security headers at all (X-Frame-Options,
  X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy) --
  only the Next.js frontend did, despite security.tsx's copy claiming
  this applies to "every response." Left /docs and /redoc unprotected
  against framing. Added a headers middleware.
- ALLOWED_ORIGINS="*" combined with allow_credentials=True (a plausible
  operator typo in Render's env vars) would silently make CORS reflect
  any origin with credentials -- app now refuses to boot with that
  combination instead.
- Three endpoints doing real, billed AI/scraping work (inspection photo
  AI analysis, the Claude marketing-copy generator, the lead-scrape
  trigger) had zero rate limiting or cost cap beyond role/plan gating --
  a compromised privileged account or a buggy retry loop had no
  built-in ceiling on Anthropic/OpenAI/Google Places billing, and on
  this single-worker server a burst could also stall every other
  tenant's requests. Added reasonable per-minute limits to all three.

Not fixed here, flagged for a follow-up decision (both require either
a schema migration or a product/UX tradeoff, not a mechanical fix):
- Password reset tokens (staff-side /auth/reset-password) are replayable
  within their 30-minute window -- not marked single-use like the
  tenant-portal equivalent already is.
- Rate limiting on login/reset/2FA is per-IP only, no per-account
  lockout/backoff -- a distributed credential-stuffing attempt across
  many source IPs isn't meaningfully throttled today.
- API keys are stored and compared in plaintext (high-entropy,
  infeasible to brute-force, but a DB-level compromise would expose
  live keys directly rather than hashes) -- hashing at rest would need
  a rotation flow since existing keys can't be un-hashed.

def handle(message: str, trace: Trace) -> str:
    hits = _get_store().search(message, k=3)
    relevant = [h for h in hits if h.score >= rag.RELEVANCE_FLOOR]

    if not relevant:
        # Grounding guarantee: no relevant doc -> abstain, don't invent.
        raise AbstainError("no knowledge-base match above relevance floor")

    context = "\n\n".join(f"[{h.doc.source}] {h.doc.text}" for h in relevant)

The native comms platform (Slices 1–6) extends the CRM in-place under `src/lib/comms/` and `/app/comms` — it is **not** a parallel marketing platform, and GoHighLevel stays **frozen** (not extended, not removed). Campaign/enrollment plumbing lives here; the *send-path compliance* details live in **twilio-a2p-compliance**.

- **Enrollment lifecycle drives the drips.** `comm_campaign_enrollments` carries a status (`enrolled`, `paused_for_conversation`, …). The drip runner (`campaign-run.ts` `dripAdvance`) selects **only** `status='enrolled'`, so pausing an enrollment removes it from the population entirely — a *structural* guarantee, not a heuristic. Reuse this lifecycle; do not build a second scheduler.
- **A reply pauses promotional automation (§10).** On a genuine inbound reply, `inbound.ts` sets that member's `enrolled` enrollments to `paused_for_conversation` (audited). This is why FSOS never sends a "haven't heard back" follow-up after a customer has engaged. Resume is deferred: the `resume-paused` cron runs the pure `evaluateResume` (`conversation-mode.ts`) against the editable `comm_conversation_policy` (quiet-period is a config default, `is_assumption`) and returns eligible enrollments to `enrolled` — on a manual resume, a resolved/closed conversation, or the customer going quiet ≥ the configured window.
- **Simulation is required before activation (§14).** A campaign cannot activate without a recent read-only simulation pass on record (`comm_campaigns.simulated_at`; activate returns **422 `simulation_required`** otherwise). Treat activation as gated on a dry-run — see **twilio-a2p-compliance** for the simulator.
- **Delegated agency-owner outreach.** Outreach on behalf of an agency owner carries an actual-sender vs represented-party model and requires an ACTIVE, in-scope delegation; unresolved ownership routes to an assignment-review queue rather than sending (ADR-015/§6). The authority check is enforced in the gate (`delegation`/`ownership` steps); the campaign/enrollment side just supplies the represented agency.

- **Build order & spine:** `docs/build-order.md`, `docs/specs/workflows-core-spine.md`, `docs/specs/workflows-ops-compliance.md`, `docs/specs/cases-commission.md`, `docs/specs/review-conversion-crosssell.md`, `docs/specs/data-api-map.md`.

explanation:
fix(comms): production-readiness review — compliance, security, correctness & docs

Comprehensive review of the AI Communications Center (6 parallel reviewers,
adversarially verified). Fixes every confirmed Critical/Important finding plus
high-value Minors, with regression tests and full docs reconciliation.

Compliance / guardrails
- Gate ordering (CRITICAL): move business_hours (a non-escalating operational
  deferral) to the deferral tail so a firewall / DNC / recommendation / delegation /
  data-confidence trip evaluated outside operating hours still escalates on its own
  step instead of being masked as a benign "held for hours" deferral (§13.9).
  Regression test added.
- Securities firewall: send.ts now OR-resolves is_security server-side from the stored
  conversation/household flag, so the one-off send route can no longer bypass the
  firewall with a client-supplied flag (defense in depth at every call site).
- DNC opt-out (CRITICAL): match tolerantly by digit suffix for SMS so a STOP stored as
  +1XXXXXXXXXX still blocks an outbound to XXXXXXXXXX (TCPA opt-out bypass).
- Consent: a channel-wide revoke is now a hard FLOOR a purpose-scoped grant cannot
  override, and STOP cascades to revoke purpose-scoped consent rows (stores stay
  consistent). Fixed the marketing-email frequency filter (.in vs raw string) that
  silently zeroed the marketing caps.
- AI authority (§11): the authority matrix + §12 evaluations now run for EVERY
  aiGenerated send, so an unclassified AI message fails safe to draft-for-human-review
  and can't bypass by omitting the class.

Security
- HTML-escape recipient-controlled merge values on the email channel (stored-XSS /
  injection defense); SMS/plaintext unchanged.
- Sign click-tracking redirect targets (HMAC, bound to the message id) and verify at
  click time — closes the open-redirect on the tracking endpoint.

Correctness / API
- Safe DB error responses across all comms routes (no raw error strings; generic
  message + server-side log) via a shared dbErrorResponse helper.
- Campaign activate: dispatch first, mark active only on success (+ re-activation
  guard) so a dispatch failure never leaves a campaign active with nothing sent.
- runIdempotent: release the claim on failure so a transient error no longer poisons
  the key into a false "already sent" idempotent skip.
- Template submit/approve + identity singleton save now check rows-affected / upsert
  (no false success); removed a dead 'admin' role from comms permission lists.
- Persist the exact transmitted body (incl. SMS TRAIGA footer) for audit fidelity.

UI / a11y
- Hub-level loading.tsx (skeleton) + error.tsx (isolated, retryable) for the comms hub.
- Campaign builder: enforce the required name (gate Next/submit + inline error).
- Subnav Overview active state; SMS casing.
- Term-conversion email: reframe product-ownership prose to conditional/educational (§4.3).

Tests
- New tests/comms-security-fixes.test.mjs (escaping + redirect signing); strengthened
  email-determinism (locks the 30-template set); guardrail gate regression for the
  ordering fix; RLS harness now proves client isolation on comm_messages/comm_conversations.

Docs / skills
- Reconciled the "7-step" → 13-step gate across the specs (canonical enumeration in
  data-guardrails.md §5); extended comms-ai-compliance.md through Slices 1–8; added the
  shipped comms routes to routes.md/sitemap.md; DESIGN.md sub-nav pattern note; new ADR
  index; Slices 7–9 skills backfill.

Authentication Bypass For Endpoints With Anonymous Access

Using a remember-me cookie with an arbitrary username can cause Opencast
to assume proper authentication for that user even if the remember-me
cookie was incorrect given that the attacked endpoint also allows
anonymous access.

This way, an attacker can, for example, fake a remember-me token, assume
the identity of the global system administrator and request non-public
content from the search service without ever providing any proper
authentication.

The reason for this problem is that using a remember-me cookie will
always cause the user in the request context to be populated, even if
the cookie is invalid by now. This is usually no problem, except in
combination with anonymous access where anonymous authentication is
granted and the request may continue.

In such a case, Opencast's security service would just check that a user
existed in the request context and assume proper authentication of this
user, never checking if it's actually anonymous authentication.

This patch adds this additional check, falling back to the anonymous
user in case of anonymous authentication.

GHSA-pxmc-2ffp-8j67: prevent arbitrary certificate revocation via duplicate DB rows

Certificate identity was tracked only by Lemur's internal database row, not
by the actual CA-side certificate. Any authenticated user could upload a
duplicate record for a certificate they didn't own (matching an existing
authority_id and serial) and then revoke it, causing the CA to revoke the
real certificate belonging to another user.

- POST /api/1/certificates/upload now requires AuthorityPermission on the
  specified authority, and rejects uploads whose (authority_id, serial)
  pair already matches an existing certificate (409).
- PUT /api/1/certificates/<id>/revoke now checks authorization and endpoint
  attachment against every certificate row sharing (authority_id, serial)
  with the one being revoked, not just the row named in the request.

GHSA-pxmc-2ffp-8j67: prevent arbitrary certificate revocation via duplicate DB rows

Certificate identity was tracked only by Lemur's internal database row, not
by the actual CA-side certificate. Any authenticated user could upload a
duplicate record for a certificate they didn't own (matching an existing
authority_id and serial) and then revoke it, causing the CA to revoke the
real certificate belonging to another user.

  specified authority, and rejects uploads whose (authority_id, serial)
  pair already matches an existing certificate (409).
- PUT /api/1/certificates/<id>/revoke now checks authorization and endpoint
  attachment against every certificate row sharing (authority_id, serial)
  with the one being revoked, not just the row named in the request.

merge: sync official main with ChatArch feature review (#39)

* Surface warning when context exceeds compression threshold but compression is blocked

Previously, when a session crossed the compression threshold but compression
was skipped (summary-LLM cooldown, #11529, or anti-thrashing, #40803), the
model kept accumulating context until it hit the hard provider token limit and
silently stopped answering — with no signal to the user about why.

Changes:
- context_compressor.should_compress_info() returns a (should_compress, reason)
  tuple. reason is 'cooldown:<seconds>' or 'ineffective' when compression is
  needed but blocked. should_compress() keeps its bool contract so existing
  callers (conversation_loop.py) and regression #29335 are unaffected.
- turn_context.build_turn_context() emits a deduped _emit_warning when the
  context is over threshold but compression is blocked, advising /new or
  /compress. Dedup keys on the block *kind* (cooldown/ineffective), not the
  ticking countdown, so a cooldown doesn't re-fire the warning every turn.
- Adds tests/agent/test_turn_context_overflow_warning.py covering the tuple
  shape, both block kinds, dedup, and re-fire-after-clear.

* Address sweeper review: safe should_compress_info + cover all guards

- ContextEngine.should_compress_info() default impl so plugin engines
  (e.g. _StubEngine) don't raise AttributeError at the call site.
- Centralise warning/reset in AIAgent._warn_context_overflow_blocked /
  _clear_context_overflow_warn so turn-context and conversation-loop guards
  share identical dedup logic and reset on the real compression boundary.
- Cover conversation_loop.py pre-API (~L1007) and loop-compaction (~L4774)
  guards, not just the turn-context preflight.
- _FakeAgent mirrors the two helpers; test suite green (219 passed).

Fixes #62708

* fix(compression): reset blocked-overflow dedup on every compression path + noise-filter survival pins

Follow-up fixes for the #62625 salvage:

- Dedup-reset gap (sweeper review): when the block clears while the
  context is STILL over threshold, execution enters the compression
  branch — the PR's 'else' reset never ran, so the warning stayed
  suppressed forever after the first block. _clear_context_overflow_warn()
  now fires on every automatic compression path: turn-context preflight,
  conversation_loop pre-API gate, and the post-tool loop-compaction gate.
- should_compress_info on current main: main refactored should_compress
  into _automatic_compression_blocked()/_locally(); the tuple variant now
  derives its reason from the same in-memory state via
  _compression_block_reason(), keeping cooldown:<s>/ineffective shapes.
- ContextEngine.should_compress_info ABC default now actually returns
  (should_compress(tokens), None) — the PR's default had a docstring but
  no return (returned None, would crash tuple-unpacking call sites).
- Below-threshold guard: the turn-context persisted-cooldown branch and
  the conversation_loop pre-API cooldown branch no longer warn when the
  estimate is under threshold (should_compress_info returns a None
  reason; the preflight pre-check is not a threshold guarantee). The
  pre-API guard also honors compression.max_attempts instead of a
  hardcoded 3, and no longer fabricates a cooldown reason.
- Noise-filter survival (#69550 composition): warning text is now a
  template constant (CONTEXT_OVERFLOW_BLOCKED_WARNING_TEMPLATE) marked
  FAILURE-CLASS, pinned un-swallowed in VISIBLE_COMPRESSION_MESSAGES and
  in new tests that execute the real _TELEGRAM_NOISY_STATUS_RE +
  _prepare_gateway_status_message.
- Contributor mapping for stanislav@local -> sl4m3.

* fix(compression): guard overflow-warn dedup reset against minimal test doubles

The dedup-reset calls assumed a full AIAgent; gateway/loop test doubles
built via object.__new__ lack _clear_context_overflow_warn and crashed
in build_turn_context (caught by test_api_content_sidecar on CI slice 3).
getattr-guard all four call sites per the established test-double pitfall
pattern (AGENTS.md #17).

* fix(compression): compose the blocked-warning probe with engine preflight

Two composition fixes vs the merged #69865 engine-preflight arm:
1. should_compress_info probe getattr-guarded — minimal compressor
   doubles (SimpleNamespace) and plugin engines lack it; absence means
   no block reason, no warning.
2. Engine maintenance hook stays un-consulted when any skip-branch
   fired (failure cooldown / deferred estimate / codex-native) —
   restoring the #20316 contract the warn-chain restructure broke.

* fix(credential-pool): exhaust all entries sharing a failed API key on 402

A 402/429/401 is an API-key–level failure (account out of balance,
rate-limited, or key rejected), but the same key can back more than one
pool entry — e.g. an explicit pool entry plus a `model_config` entry
auto-seeded from `model.api_key`, both carrying the identical
`runtime_api_key`.

`mark_exhausted_and_rotate(api_key_hint=...)` only marked the *first*
matching entry, leaving the sibling OK. `_select_unlocked()` then kept
handing back the same depleted key, so the billing-recovery `continue`
loop in the conversation retry path never converged: the request hung
until the client disconnected (~2.5min observed against DeepSeek),
emitting only `response.created` with no 402 ever surfaced to the user.

Mark every entry sharing the failed key so the pool can reach the
"no available entries" state and let the error propagate immediately.

Adds a regression test covering two entries backed by the same key.

* perf(credential-pool): persist same-key sibling exhaustion once

Follow-up to the #68565 salvage: batch the sibling _mark_exhausted calls
behind a single _persist() instead of one auth.json write per sibling.

* chore(contributors): add email mapping for airclear

* fix(update): survive undeletable untracked files during autostash (#70161)

git stash push --include-untracked exits non-zero when it saved
everything but could not DELETE some swept untracked files from the
working tree (e.g. a root-owned packaging/ directory left behind by a
sudo'd build: 'warning: failed to remove ...: Permission denied').
The updater ran the push with check=True, so this benign partial
failure raised CalledProcessError and aborted the whole update before
it even fetched — reliably, on every run, for any user with an
undeletable untracked path in the checkout.

Fix, both ends of the class:
- _stash_local_changes_if_needed: probe refs/stash before/after the
  push. Non-zero push + fresh stash entry = changes are saved; warn,
  reset the tracked-side leftovers (they're in the stash), and
  continue the update. Non-zero push + NO stash entry = real failure;
  keep aborting.
- _restore_stashed_changes: on restore, those same undeletable files
  still sit in the tree, so 'git stash apply' exits 1 with 'already
  exists, no checkout' even though every tracked change applied and
  nothing was lost. Classify that stderr shape (strictly — any other
  error line still routes to the conflict path) as restored instead
  of resetting the tree and telling the user the restore failed.

Repro'd both halves with real git; behavioral E2E test covers
stash -> checkout -> restore round-trip with an undeletable dir.

* fix(credential-pool): stop lost-update cooldown erasure and wrong-key quarantine

Two related races in credential-pool cooldown state:

1. Lost update across processes: write_credential_pool merged only
   entries missing from the caller's snapshot; for entries present on
   both sides the caller's in-memory copy won wholesale. A process
   holding a snapshot taken before another process marked a key
   exhausted would, on its next persist (e.g. a round-robin rotation),
   write the key back as healthy — erasing the cooldown so every
   process resumes hammering a rate-limited key. Merge status fields by
   last_status_at recency: adopt the on-disk status only when it is
   strictly newer AND still binding (DEAD, or EXHAUSTED with an
   unexpired cooldown), and never onto re-authed (token-changed)
   entries, so legitimate expiry-clears and fresh logins are preserved.

2. Wrong-key quarantine: when mark_exhausted_and_rotate received an
   api_key_hint that matched no entry, it fell through to
   current()/_select_unlocked() — on a freshly loaded pool that selects
   the NEXT healthy key and benches it for the full cooldown TTL,
   punishing an innocent credential. When a hint is provided but
   unmatched, rotate without marking anything instead of guessing.

* fix(kanban): stop decompose siblings sharing one worktree checkout

Decompose children inherit the root's literal workspace_path (#37172),
so every sibling of a worktree-kind root points at the SAME checkout.
_resolve_worktree_workspace's existing-checkout shortcut then reuses
that directory on whatever branch is currently checked out, ignoring
the task's own branch_name. Net effect: sibling workers — which can be
promoted and dispatched concurrently — run in one directory on the
first sibling's branch, with no lock. Work lands on the wrong task's
branch (provenance corruption) and concurrent siblings trample each
other's index/tree.

Fix, two layers:
- decompose_triage_task: worktree-kind children no longer inherit the
  root's literal path; each child materializes its own
  <repo>/.worktrees/<child-id> at dispatch (dir/scratch inheritance
  unchanged — children legitimately share those).
- _resolve_worktree_workspace: when the requested path is an existing
  checkout of a DIFFERENT branch, fall back to a fresh
  <repo>/.worktrees/<task-id> instead of silently reusing it (heals
  rows that already carry a shared path). Same-branch reuse and the
  no-repo/own-path degenerate cases keep the legacy behaviour.

* fix(credential_pool): acquire the pool lock in has_available/peek/current/entries

`has_available()`, `peek()`, `current()` and `entries()` read (and, via
`_available_entries()`, mutate and persist) `self._entries` without holding
`self._lock`, while every other entry point — `select()`,
`mark_exhausted_and_rotate()`, `acquire_lease()`, `try_refresh_current()` —
guards the exact same access with the lock.

`_available_entries()` is not read-only: it prunes aged-out DEAD manual
entries (rebinding `self._entries` at the prune step) and calls `_persist()`
(writes auth.json). The gateway runs platform adapters in threads and cron
runs jobs in a ThreadPoolExecutor, so a status probe via `has_available()`
or `peek()` can race a concurrent `select()`/rotation: torn iteration of
`self._entries`, interleaved auth.json writes, or a lost token rotation.

Fix: take `self._lock` in all four query methods. Because the lock is
non-reentrant and `peek()` composes `current()` + `_available_entries()`,
add a lock-free `_current_unlocked()` helper and route the already-locked
internal callers (`_select_unlocked`, `mark_exhausted_and_rotate`,
`_try_refresh_current_unlocked`) through it to avoid self-deadlock.

Added regression tests: a no-deadlock check (peek re-entrancy) and a
lock-held-blocks-the-call check for each of the four methods.

* fix(credential_pool): complete the locking boundary across the public pool surface

Follow-up to review feedback:

- Acquire self._lock in the remaining public pool-state methods:
  has_credentials, reset_statuses, remove_index, resolve_target, and
  add_entry. All of them read or rebind self._entries (and the mutating
  ones persist auth.json), so they now hold the same lock as select()
  and the query methods. None are called from within the lock, so no
  unlocked helpers are needed.
- Make the blocking test deterministic: an instrumented lock records the
  acquire attempt, and the test first waits for the worker to actually
  reach self._lock before asserting it blocks. Previously an unlocked
  method could pass if the worker thread was scheduled late.
- Extend the lock test matrix to all nine public methods; the five newly
  locked ones fail the test without this fix.

* fix: resolve current entry unlocked in try_refresh_matching no-hint branch

* fix(windows): hidden-console daemons — extend the parent-console fix to every detached spawn path (#70205)

Extends the desktop backend's root-cause fix (aa2ae36c3f) to all remaining
console-less parent launch paths. The Windows console-flash class
(#54220/#56747) is governed by the PARENT's console: a DETACHED_PROCESS or
pythonw.exe daemon has no console, so every console-subsystem descendant
(git, gh, cmd, node, wmic, powershell) allocates its own visible conhost —
one flash per spawn, unreachable by any per-call-site CREATE_NO_WINDOW
sweep. Worse, MSDN specifies CREATE_NO_WINDOW is IGNORED when combined
with DETACHED_PROCESS, so the hide bit in the old detach bundle was dead.

Changes:

  and windows_detach_flags_without_breakaway(); the daemon now owns a
  single hidden console (CREATE_NO_WINDOW) that all descendants inherit.

  premise only held while DETACHED_PROCESS was masking the hide bit);

- gateway/run.py: restart watcher keeps sys.executable instead of

- web_server: dashboard actions spawn sys.executable (already carries

* fix(auxiliary): treat explicit model:auto sentinel, not just cfg_model

'auto' is a sentinel meaning "inherit from main runtime / auto-detect",
not a literal model id -- already handled for cfg_model (config-derived)
in _resolve_task_provider_model, but not for the explicit `model` kwarg.

MoA reference/aggregator slots (agent/moa_loop.py's _slot_runtime) forward
a preset's `model:` field as this explicit argument rather than through
auxiliary.<task> config, so a MoA preset configured with `model: auto`
(a natural thing to try given the existing auxiliary.*.model: auto
convention) reached this function as the explicit `model` arg and took
the `model or cfg_model` branch, bypassing the cfg_model-only sentinel
check entirely -- sending the literal string "auto" to the wire as a
model id.

Normalize both the explicit `model` and `cfg_model` the same way, fixing
this at the single chokepoint every caller (MoA included) already goes
through, rather than patching moa_loop.py separately.

* fix(moa): pass custom extra_body to slots

* fix(gateway): honor explicit api_server enabled:false under env key

_apply_env_overrides() force-set ``api_server.enabled = True`` whenever
API_SERVER_KEY (or API_SERVER_ENABLED) was present in the environment.

In multiplex mode, a secondary profile pins
``platforms.api_server.enabled: false`` in its config.yaml so that it
shares the default profile's API-server listener instead of binding its
own port. That profile still inherits the process-level env, including
API_SERVER_KEY, so the unconditional re-enable flipped api_server back on
and tripped the MultiplexConfigError check.

Honor an explicit disable, flagged by ``_enabled_explicit`` in the
platform's extra. Use ``extra.pop("_enabled_explicit", False)``: the
api_server branch is terminal (unlike the migrated plugin platforms, no
later registry pass re-enables api_server), so popping consumes the flag
in a single read and avoids the double-read hazard, while the final
per-platform cleanup remains a no-op.

with api_server explicitly enabled:false + _enabled_explicit:true survives
_apply_env_overrides() as enabled=False (fails without the fix), while the
key is still wired through for the shared listener.

* fix(slack): add catch-all event handler to prevent Slack auto-disabling Event Subscriptions

Without a catch-all handler, slack-bolt returns HTTP 404 for every
unhandled bot event (user_change, user_huddle_changed, reaction_added,
etc.) and never sends the Socket Mode ack. On active Slack workspaces
where the app is subscribed to high-volume events, this produces a
near-100% un-acked failure rate that crosses Slack's >95%/60-min
threshold and triggers automatic disabling of the app's Event

handlers so bolt's router matches those first. Truly unhandled events
are silently acked (200) and logged at DEBUG. The failure rate stays
near 0% regardless of which events the Slack app manifest subscribes to.

* fix(slack): neutralize prompt injection in thread-context backfill

`SlackAdapter._fetch_thread_context` formats each prior thread message as
`{name}: {msg_text}` and joins them with newlines into the block the call
site prepends *raw* into the model turn (`text = thread_context + text`).
Both fields are attacker-influenceable — any thread participant sets their
own Slack display name and message text — and neither was neutralized, so
an embedded newline let a thread message break out of its line and pose as
a fresh markdown section (a fake "## SYSTEM" / "## Override" heading) inside
the context the model reads when first mentioned mid-thread.

This is the same indirect-prompt-injection vector already closed for the
sibling untrusted sinks: the sender-name prefix
(`neutralize_untrusted_inline_text`), the reply quote, and the relay
channel-context renderer. The Slack thread-context backfill — the default
whenever the bot is mentioned in a thread with no active session — was the
missed sink. (The existing `[unverified]` tagging marks *who* a message is
from; it does nothing about newline structure, so an authorized sender can
inject just as easily.)

Flatten both fields with `neutralize_untrusted_inline_text` before
interpolation. The body uses `max_chars=0` so message text is not truncated
(thread context caps the message *count*, never per-message length); the
display name keeps the default bound. `parent_text` keeps the raw message
(its own reply-context sink neutralizes separately). A well-behaved message
is preserved byte-for-byte.

Adds a regression test covering a hostile display name, a hostile message
body, benign passthrough, and the no-truncation guarantee.

* fix(slack): stop double-decoding HTML entities when escaping message text

format_message unescapes already-escaped input before re-escaping, so that
pre-escaped text doesn't get double-escaped. That unescape was three
sequential str.replace calls, which re-scan each other's output:

    "&lt;"  --(& -> &)-->  "<"  --(< -> <)-->  "<"

The & produced by the first replace pairs with the following "lt;" and
decodes a second time. "&lt;" is the wire form of the literal text
"<", so the text is silently destroyed: Slack receives "<" and renders
"<". Anyone writing about HTML or markup ("&lt;b&gt;" -> "<b>")
loses their literal text, with no error.

re.sub scans left-to-right and never re-scans its own replacements, so a
single pass fixes it. The escape pass on the next line is left untouched --
it is correctly ordered (& first, so the &s it inserts aren't re-escaped).

Only the double-decode cases change; every other input is byte-identical
before and after. This is the same round-trip invariant the neighbouring
test_pre_escaped_{ampersand,lt,gt}_not_double_escaped tests already assert,
extended to the case they miss. Affects the plain mrkdwn path (send,
edit_message) and Block Kit sections, which route section text through
format_message.

* fix(gateway): strip language tag from Slack fenced code blocks

Slack's mrkdwn does not strip the optional language tag from fenced
code blocks like GitHub-flavored markdown does — it renders
```text\nfoo\n``` as a code block whose literal first line is "text".
The agent emitted ```text fences around raw command output, which
surfaced "text" as the first line of every such block.

Drop the tag from the opening fence in format_message() before stashing
the block behind a placeholder. Stripping only fires for a genuine
opening fence — a ``` at the start of a line, tagged with a single
token (no spaces or backticks) — and the original line ending is
preserved. The fence-protection regex deliberately matches loosely, so
a mid-line ``` (e.g. an inline ```span``` wrapping across a newline)
can be grouped as an "opening fence" whose first line is real content;
differential fuzzing against the pre-change formatter (40k generated
messages) confirms the only behavioral delta is the tag strip itself.

The Block Kit renderer is unaffected: render_blocks() intercepts fences
itself before mrkdwn_fn is applied, so this only changes the mrkdwn
surfaces that still go through format_message() — the plain-text
fallback field (notifications, search indexing, accessibility),
slash-command ephemeral replies, and standalone cron delivery.

* fix(slack): add bold-text zero-width-space guard for trailing non-word chars

Slack's mrkdwn parser can fail to recognize the closing * of a bold span
when it is immediately preceded by a non-word character (), ], }, ., :,
em-dash, ...), mis-rendering the span and in reported cases truncating
the rest of the message.  Insert a zero-width space (U+200B) between the
last character and the closing * whenever the last character is not
alphanumeric or underscore.

ExamDetailPage rendered a login-gated placeholder (identical hardcoded
stat boxes on every page) to anonymous visitors, which is what Googlebot
sees since the site is statically exported with no live session at build

from sitemap.xml — they contradicted robots.txt and added no unique
content.

* Enable native push notifications and fix Google Sign-In for local builds

Firebase project is now configured (google-services.json obtained from
console) so the native push registration that was disabled after the
login-crash root-cause fix can be safely restored — PushNotifications
.register() no longer throws on missing FirebaseApp init.

- Commit google-services.json (no secret values; the API key is
  restricted by Android package name and ships inside every built APK
  regardless, so gitignoring it only bought inconsistent CI builds)
- Reinstall @capacitor/push-notifications, restore its config block and
  FCM token registration logic (registration/error/received/action
  listeners, permission request, register())
- Re-sync Android native project (5 plugins now, was 4)
- Add NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID to frontend/.env.production using the
  Web OAuth client Firebase auto-created for the Google sign-in provider,
  so local Windows builds get working Google Sign-In like CI builds
  already do via the REACT_APP_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID GitHub secret

* Fix Google Client ID mismatch: use the client already wired to backend

The Firebase-auto-created Web client (from google-services.json) is a
different OAuth client than the one backend/GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID on Render
actually expects — its default redirect URIs are Firebase's own auth
handler, not this app's /auth/google/callback. Swapped
NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID in .env.production to match Render's
GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID so local Windows builds are consistent with backend.

def clean_username(self, username, request):
    if not request.user.is_authenticated:
        raise PermissionDenied('Authentication required')
        """
        Allow the backend to clean the username, if the backend defines a
        clean_username method.
        """
        backend_str = request.session[auth.BACKEND_SESSION_KEY]
        backend = auth.load_backend(backend_str)
        try:

        except AttributeError:  # Backend has no clean_username method.
            pass
        return username

    async def aclean_username(self, username, request):

        backend_str = await request.session.aget(auth.BACKEND_SESSION_KEY)

        try:

Allowlist link schemes, sweep every route for IDOR, drop product names

Fixes a real cross-site scripting hole in compiled output. Link hrefs were
escaped but their scheme was never checked, so a document containing
javascript:alert(1) produced a working anchor in every format that carries
links. Escaping cannot help there: the payload contains nothing that needs
escaping. isSafeHref now allowlists http, https, mailto and relative
references, normalising away case, whitespace and control characters first so
JaVaScRiPt: and an embedded tab do not slip past, and failing closed on schemes
nobody has listed. An unsafe link loses its anchor, keeps its text, and warns.
Markdown gets the same treatment, since markdown links execute in renderers.

IdorSweepTest enumerates every route from the handler mapping and drives each
one with a stranger's token. Routes naming another account's resource must not
answer 2xx; caller-scoped collections may, but must not contain the victim's
data; nothing may answer 500; and the victim's project must be unchanged
afterwards. Reading the mapping rather than a hand-written list means a new
controller method that forgets its authorization check fails immediately.

Removes third-party product names from tracked files, replacing them with
descriptions of the behaviour they referred to.

190 Java and 95 Node tests green. Verified by mutation: making the ownership
check pass for everyone turns the sweep red.

Blank product pages, one icon family, and the pre-launch gate (#174)

* login: make OTP code boxes light (visible digits on the light auth page)

The code-entry boxes used the dark theme (bg-space-black + white text), but
the storefront login page is light — so the boxes rendered near-black and the
typed digits were invisible. Switch to white boxes with slate-900 digits, a
grey border and a violet focus ring to match the light page.

* admin: action-item count badges in the sidebar (open tickets, pending payments, orders to fulfil)

New GET /api/admin/nav-counts returns open-ticket / pending-payment-proof /
paid-order-awaiting-fulfilment counts; AdminLayout shows a fuchsia badge next
to Support, Payments and Fulfillment (refetched on navigation + every 60s), so
a new ticket is visible at a glance instead of having to hunt for it.

* Per-category delivery explanation on product pages + Discord

Answers the #1 pre-purchase question ('how do I get it?') right on each
product, and mirrors it in Discord.

- src/lib/deliveryInfo.js: bilingual (EN/NL) delivery info per category —
  Robux (Group Payout / Roblox+ method: enable 2FA, 5000 R$/day limit so
  large orders split across days, very large via 2 staff accounts),
  V-Bucks (gift-card code), and a solid code/top-up default.
- ProductDetail: a 'How this is delivered' panel (method + numbered steps +
  good-to-know notes), light-theme styled, with NL labels.
- Discord: /price now shows the delivery method; new /delivery command gives
  the full steps + notes; registered + added to /help.

* admin: one-click suggested sell price from supplier cost

Enter the cost you pay (e.g. on Eldorado/Eneba) and get a 'Suggest price'
button that applies a ~18% markup with a €2 minimum profit, rounded to a
clean .99 — so €140 cost → €165.99, €10 → €11.99. Tune MARKUP/FLOOR in one
place. Existing margin readout stays.

* delivery: drop the Roblox-group join step from Robux (group is only for giveaways)

Robux delivery no longer mentions joining a Roblox group — the group is used
for giveaways, not delivery. Steps are now: enable 2FA → send your username →

* Fix 5 bugs found in a full site + Discord audit

Frontend
- Checkout page crashed on render: the main component called t() dozens of
  times but never ran useI18n() (only the helper sub-components did), so the
  whole checkout threw a ReferenceError the moment the cart had items. Nobody
  could reach the pay step. Added const { t } = useI18n().

Server
- Gift-card codes were derived purely from Date.now() mod 32, so only 32
  distinct codes could ever be generated — trivially guessable/enumerable
  (drain any outstanding card via the public balance check + redeem) and
  colliding on the UNIQUE index after a few issues. Now generated with
  crypto.randomInt over a 32-char alphabet (~10^24 space); proven 20000/20000
  unique.
- Manual-payment proof confirm/reject never notified the buyer: it checked
  order.user_id, but getOrder() hydrates to camelCase order.userId, so the
  guard was always false. Fixed both call sites; the reject email's order link
  was also an empty string — now points at the public track page.

Discord bot
- Auto-moderation + XP ran inside CLAIMED tickets: claiming renames the
  channel to '✋-ticket-…', which defeated the startsWith('ticket-') check, so
  a customer pasting a trade link in their own claimed ticket got their
  message deleted and publicly warned. Detect tickets by their stable
  'ticket-owner:' topic (survives the rename) via a shared isTicketChannel().
- /suggest could report 'interaction failed' while actually posting: it did
  two Discord round-trips (send + startThread) before its first reply, risking
  the 3s ACK window. Now defers first, then edits the reply.

* Fix slow first request (cold start): defer non-critical boot work

Symptom: signup / 'send code' could take ~15s. Cause: ensureReady() — which the
serverless handler awaits before EVERY request on a cold instance — ran heavy
upkeep synchronously on each boot: ~11 email-template queries, per-product art
backfill across the whole catalog (~70+ products), and starter-content dedupe.
On a cold Neon connection those ~100 sequential round-trips stacked up before
the request (and its OTP email) even started.

Now ensureReady only awaits what a request truly needs — migrate (schema),
seed on an empty DB, and stocking an empty catalog — and defers the rest
(syncEmailTemplates upgrade, seedStarterContent, syncCatalogImages) to a
one-shot background task that runs after we're ready to serve.

Measured locally: on an already-seeded DB the blocking boot dropped from doing
~100 queries to 3 (~36ms); on cold Neon that removes the multi-second stall.
The empty-DB path is unchanged (seed() still installs roles/permissions/all
templates synchronously, so auth + OTP work on the very first request).

Verified: boot e2e (6 checks — roles, catalog and login_otp template ready
immediately; 2nd ensureReady memoised; starter box + bundle appear via
background upkeep). Regression (19), lint, build green.

* Supplier listing URLs + serial one-order-at-a-time fulfillment queue

Extends supplier auto-fulfillment so the owner can paste a listing link (e.g. an
Eldorado URL) and paid orders are sourced strictly one at a time, oldest first.

- Migration 021: supplier_products.supplier_url. mapSupplierProduct stores it,
  the admin mapping route + Suppliers.jsx get a 'Listing URL' field, and the
  mapping list shows/links it. The URL is passed into the connector's
  createFulfillment (EldoradoConnector forwards it as listingUrl).
- Serial queue (fulfillmentService): on payment, instead of firing a per-order
  fulfillment, we drain a queue that processes paid supplier orders ONE AT A
  TIME, oldest first — finishing (buy + deliver) one before starting the next.
  A short DB lease (kv row + TTL) guarantees only one worker drains at a time
  across serverless instances; an 'attempted' set advances past orders that open
  no request (margin-guarded) instead of looping; async in-progress buys are
  re-polled from maintenance. Also drained from maintenance as a safety net.

Reality note kept honest in the UI copy: a bare marketplace link can only be
auto-purchased when the connector has a real buy API (Eldorado apiKey); the
queue + link plumbing makes it fully automatic the moment that's configured.

Verified on real Postgres: serial-queue e2e (8 checks — URL stored + passed to
the connector, three paid orders bought strictly oldest-first one at a time, all
completed, a second drain skips under the lease, no double-buying) and the
supplier auto-fulfill e2e (10 checks, incl. the margin-guard order no longer
stalls the queue). Regression (19), lint, build green.

* Add real auto-buy via Kinguin connector (Eldorado.gg has no buyer API)

Researched the request against the actual APIs:
- Eldorado.gg (the P2P marketplace) publishes NO public BUYER API — its API is
  seller-side only, so you cannot programmatically purchase another seller's
  listing. Auto-buying from a bare Eldorado link isn't possible via an official
  API. The Eldorado connector hint now says so plainly.
- Kinguin DOES publish a documented dropship/order API. Built a KinguinConnector
  that plugs into the existing connector interface + serial queue:
    createFulfillment → POST /v1/order  (X-Api-Key, products:[{kinguinId,qty,price}], orderExternalId)
    checkFulfillment  → GET  /v2/order/{id}         (status)
                        GET  /v2/order/{id}/keys     (real serials → deliveries)
  No upfront payment (charged on the buyer's purchase); async delivery is
  handled by the queue's re-poll. Registered as connector kind 'kinguin' and
  added to the admin supplier dropdown. The fulfilment request now passes the
  mapping cost so the order price is set.

Verified: KinguinConnector unit test with mocked fetch (16 checks — exact
POST /v1/order body incl. kinguinId/qty/price/orderExternalId + X-Api-Key,
in_progress→completed poll, real serial mapped to a delivery, shadow/off via
autoDeliver:false, registry knows the kind). Serial-queue (8) + regression (19),
lint and build green.

Sources: github.com/kinguinltdhk/Kinguin-eCommerce-API (order v1/v2 + keys).

Researched G2A and Eneba against their real APIs:
- G2A publishes a documented Integration/Import order API → built G2AConnector:
    add    POST /v3/order          { product_id, currency, max_price }
    pay    PUT  /v3/order/pay      { order_id }
    key    GET  /v3/order/key/{id} → { key }
  Auth header 'Authorization: {apiHash}, {sha256(apiHash+email+apiKey)}'.
  max_price is capped at our stored cost so it never buys above our price.
  Registered as connector kind 'g2a' + added to the admin dropdown; async key
  delivery handled by the serial queue's re-poll.
- Eneba: merchant/seller GraphQL API only (no public buyer purchase) — not built.
- Eldorado.gg: seller-only, no buyer API (already noted).

So real auto-buy is now available for Kinguin AND G2A (game keys / gift cards);
Robux/V-Bucks-style P2P top-ups have no legal buy API anywhere and stay manual.

Verified: G2AConnector unit test with mocked fetch (13 checks — exact auth hash,
add-order body incl. product_id/currency/max_price, pay step, key→delivery,
refunded→failed, shadow/off, registry knows the kind). Regression (19), lint,

* Audit round: fix payment, coin, and supplier auto-buy money/security bugs

Full audit of the manual-payments, supplier auto-buy, Forge+/coins/wallet,
trust-stats, cold-start and security surfaces. Stats, cold-start, DB
parameterization, admin authz and secret handling verified solid; the
confirmed defects below are fixed and covered by e2e tests.

Payments
- orderService: make the order status transition atomic (conditional UPDATE
  guarded on the observed status + change check). Concurrent confirms / a
  webhook racing a manual confirm can no longer dispense, email or complete an
  order twice.
- paymentProofService: atomically claim a proof (UPDATE ... WHERE status=
  'pending') so a double-click / second admin can't drive a second
  markPaymentReceived; reject non-http(s) screenshot links (zod .url() also
  passes javascript:/data:, a stored-XSS vector in the admin queue); flag the
  2nd proof as multiple_submissions (was off-by-one at the 3rd).
- catalog: reject the screenshot URL at the route too; disable the demo
  self-pay route whenever a real payment method is configured.
- Checkout: show the server order total on the pay-instructions screen — the
  cart is cleared first, so the old cart-derived amount read €0.00.

Forge Coins / membership
- forgeCoinService: lock the user row (FOR UPDATE) before summing in
  spendCoins/redeemReward/grantCoins, matching walletService. Concurrent
  spends can no longer both pass the balance check (negative balance / free
  rewards / free membership).
- account: charge + grant membership in one transaction (no "charged without
  membership", no partial grant).

Supplier auto-buy
- Kinguin/Eldorado: never mark an order fulfilled with zero delivered keys —
  a transient error fetching the keys kept the order in_progress to re-poll
  instead of completing it empty-handed (paid supplier, buyer got nothing).
- fulfillment margin guard: treat an unknown (null) supplier cost as
  do-not-auto-buy, and compare cost to the buyer's effective post-discount
  revenue per unit instead of list price (no blind uncapped buys, no buying at
  a loss on discounted orders).
- G2A: fix the doubled /v3 path prefix (every call 404'd), pass order
  quantity with a line-level max_price cap, and collect multiple keys.

* Semi-automate fulfillment: auto-surface paid orders, enrich the manual queue

Turns the "manual" tier into a semi-automatic one and closes a gap where paid
orders that can't be delivered automatically could sit invisible.

Automatic (unchanged): local code-stock auto-dispense and Kinguin/G2A supplier
auto-buy still deliver hands-off.

Auto-surface (new)
- fulfillmentService.ensureManualFulfillment: a paid order with no stock and no
  auto-supplier (e.g. a P2P Robux/V-Bucks top-up) is now queued for hand
  delivery instead of sitting at payment_received with no fulfillment request.
  Advances the order to awaiting_fulfillment (same path fulfillOrder walks) so
  completing the manual request can legally complete the order. Idempotent.
- Wired into the payment_received handler (after stock + supplier drain) and
  into maintenance as a backfill sweep (sweepUnfulfilledPaidOrders) for orders
  paid before this path existed or missed by an interrupted drain.

Semi-automatic manual queue
- listManualQueue now returns, per request: the supplier listing URL to buy
  from (supplier_url), the quantity, and the buyer's delivery target captured
  at checkout. Admin Fulfillment page shows a "Buy from supplier" link, the
  quantity, and the copy-able delivery target — buy, paste the code, one click
  delivers + e-mails the buyer.
- Capture the delivery target at checkout: products can define a deliveryField
  label (e.g. "Roblox username", set in the admin product form); Checkout shows
  a required field only when a cart item needs it and stores it on the order,
  sanitized server-side.

Robustness
- resolveFulfillmentSupplier skips a supplier whose connector kind is unknown/
  removed instead of throwing, so one bad supplier row can't abort the drain
  for every order.

Verified on local Postgres: new semi-auto e2e 10/10 (auto-surface, queue shows
buy link + qty + target, one-click deliver completes + records, idempotent),
supplier 10/10, queue 8/8, regression 19/19, npm run build green.

* Surface margin-guarded orders for review + Discord bot audit fixes

Margin-guarded orders (server)

  unknown or >= effective revenue), the order is now queued for hand delivery
  via a shared queueForHandDelivery helper instead of being left with no

Discord bot (audit findings)
- /vouch could push unlimited 5-star reviews to the storefront: externalId was
  keyed to the interaction id, defeating the server-side dedup. Now keyed to
  the user (one site review per member) plus a 1-hour per-user cooldown.
- Giveaway duration clamped to 1 min - 14 days: larger values overflow Node's

- Live price list: stop adding embed fields near Discord's 6000-char total cap

- Ticket "one open ticket" check now matches the owner id with its trailing

- getProducts: 8s fetch timeout + cache-stamped backoff so a hanging API can't
  stall every /price, /ask and price-list refresh with piled-up sockets.
- Review ingest: stop sending the raw shared secret as a legacy header; the
  HMAC-signed path is the only transport.

Verified: margin-queue e2e 5/5 (order surfaces with buy link, drain stops
re-picking, no auto duplicates), supplier 10/10, queue 8/8, semiauto 10/10,
regression 19/19, audit-fix 9/9, npm run build green, node --check on bot files.

* Email security + reliability fixes, cart-sync race, silent sign-in repair

Email (audit findings)
- renderTokens now HTML-escapes every token value unless the token name ends
  in Html (itemsHtml, deliveriesHtml, paymentHtml, noteHtml, codeHtml — all
  server-built with their own escaping). Previously billing.full_name flowed
  raw into branded emails, letting a guest checkout deliver attacker HTML to
  any address from our verified sender (phishing relay). billing.full_name and
  city are also bounded at order creation.
- deliverOrder: sending codes to an ALREADY completed order (replacement code)
  now emails the customer explicitly — the completed→completed transition
  early-returns, so the codes previously landed silently with no email/DM.
- retryFailedEmails maintenance sweep: transactional emails that failed on a
  transient provider error are re-sent from their persisted context (atomic
  claim, capped attempts per recipient so a dead address ages out). Wired as
  maintenance step 10. Previously a 10s Resend timeout on order_completed
  meant a guest never received their codes and nothing ever retried.
- assertProductionConfig: no more false "emails not delivered" warning when
  Resend is configured without SMTP_URL.

Frontend (audit findings)
- CartContext: the server-cart mirror now waits until the login restore has
  settled (a slow cold-start GET raced the 900ms mirror, which PUT an empty
  local cart over the saved one), and the restore uses a functional update so
  an item added while the GET was in flight is never replaced by a stale
  server cart.
- AuthContext: a stale fm_token no longer strands a returning customer as a
  guest — on a failed /me the token is cleared and the silent sign-in ladder
  (refresh cookie, then trusted device) is retried.
- i18n: NL translations for the checkout delivery-target field
  (checkout.deliveryPh / checkout.deliveryHint).

Verified: new email-fix e2e 11/11 (escaping + *Html passthrough, injected
full_name recorded escaped, retry sweep claims + re-sends exactly once,
replacement delivery emails again), regression 19/19, supplier 10/10, queue
8/8, semiauto 10/10, marginqueue 5/5, npm run build green.

* Self-healing Discord invite: bot maintains a permanent link, site serves it live

A default Discord invite expires after 7 days — a dead link on the storefront
silently kills community sign-ups. This closes that hole end to end:

Bot

  the most public channel it can invite from, then pushes it to the site over

- POST /api/discord/invite (HMAC-signed, replay-windowed): accepts only real

Frontend

  hardcoded link (the Discord page already read it from the API).

explanation:
fix(hotkey): verify listener PID ownership, scope process management (YAO-341) (#31)

* fix(hotkey): verify listener PID ownership, scope process management (YAO-341)

Revalidates the macOS F2 lifecycle against current macOS/Python/PyObjC. No new
hotkey or playback behavior; every change fixes a compatibility or safety
defect found by probing the running system.

- Stale-PID / PID reuse. `listener_alive()` accepted any live PID in
  listener.pid. After an unclean kill the pidfile survives and the OS recycles
  that number onto an unrelated process, at which point the supervisor sees
  "alive", skips the respawn, and F2 stays dead until the file is removed by
  hand. Reproduced: writing the pytest PID into listener.pid reported
  listener_alive=True. `coord` now confirms the PID's command line actually
  names voice_buddy.hotkey_listener, and fails open when `ps` is unreadable so
  an ambiguous probe can never kill or duplicate a healthy listener.
  `get_listener_pid` verifies the same before returning a signal target.

- Unsafe process guidance. The troubleshooting table told users to run
  `pkill -f hotkey_listener`. That matches on command line: a live check on
  this machine matched five processes, one of them unrelated to Voice Buddy.
  Replaced with `voice-buddy hotkey-restart`, which resolves the PID through
  the pidfile, verifies ownership, sends SIGTERM, and clears a stale record so
  the next SessionStart starts clean.

- Stale dependency advice. `hotkey_doctor` still told users to install
  `pyobjc-framework-Quartz>=10.0,<12.0` after YAO-339 raised the cap to `<13`,
  so anyone following it reinstalled the version the project had moved off. A
  test now pins the advice to the range pyproject declares.

Adds tests/test_hotkey_lifecycle.py (39 tests): recycled-PID rejection through
the supervisor respawn, ownership probe accept/fail-open/gone cases, multiple
concurrent sessions with independent teardown, session-id path-escape
containment, no-op supervisor on linux/win32/freebsd, and a guard that every
non-hotkey module imports with pyobjc absent — executed in a private namespace
rather than by evicting sys.modules entries, which corrupted unrelated tests.

Existing coord/session-lifecycle tests used the pytest PID as a stand-in
listener, which the ownership check correctly rejects; they now stub the probe
explicitly so the substitution is visible rather than incidental.

* fix(hotkey): tri-state ownership, verified signal gate, version-drift handoff (YAO-341)

Addresses the three blocking review items on PR #31.

- Ownership is now a tri-state verdict: OWNED / FOREIGN / UNKNOWN. The
  previous probe returned True when `ps` was unavailable, and
  `get_listener_pid()` handed that straight to `os.kill` as authorization —
  the opposite of the "fail open so we never kill the wrong process" claim in
  my delivery note. Reproduced: with `ps` raising and a recycled pidfile,
  `voice-buddy hotkey-restart` delivered SIGTERM to an unrelated live PID.

  The asymmetry is now explicit. Spawn/liveness decisions may treat UNKNOWN as
  "probably alive" — the cost is a stale hotkey. Signal decisions require
  OWNED, so no evidence means no signal target.

- `reload_listener_config()` had no ownership check at all: it read the pidfile
  and sent SIGHUP, or SIGTERM on version drift, directly. It backs `on`, `off`
  and the hotkey config commands, so a recycled PID was signalled from three
  user-facing paths. It now routes through `get_listener_pid()` like every
  other call site.

- Version drift left two listeners. The supervisor saw the mismatch, deleted
  the pid/version artifacts and spawned a replacement without terminating the
  old process, which kept its EventTap and — because session markers still
  existed — never hit its idle timer. `_retire_superseded_listener()` now runs
  inside the same coord lock, signals only a verified-OWNED PID, and waits for
  it to exit before cleanup and spawn. If it will not die, no replacement is
  started: one stale hotkey is better than two EventTaps competing for F2.

Also fixes a latent bug found while building the AC15 test: a zombie answers
`kill(pid, 0)`, so `_process_alive()` reported an exited-but-unreaped listener
as live. The handoff would then wait the full timeout and refuse to spawn,
leaving the user with no listener after an upgrade.

Adds 20 tests: tri-state probe verdicts, zero-signal proofs for
hotkey-restart / reload / on / off / signal_listener / retire under `ps`
OSError, SubprocessError and TimeoutExpired, the single-listener AC15 handoff
with real processes, the will-not-die refusal, and zombie liveness.

Existing fixtures stubbed `_process_is_listener`, which signal paths no longer
consult; they now stub `process_ownership`.

* fix(hotkey): escalate to SIGKILL when the run loop defers SIGTERM (YAO-341)

Found by running the handoff against a real listener rather than a sleeping
stand-in: SIGTERM was still pending 2.75s after delivery, and the process only
exited when the run loop's 30s timer tick let CPython run the handler. The
listener blocks in CFRunLoopRun(), so a graceful signal is observed up to a
full tick late.

A 2s budget therefore timed out on every upgrade, and the handoff refused to
spawn a replacement — leaving the user with no listener at all. Waiting a full
tick instead is not an option inside SessionStart.

The handoff now gives SIGTERM a 2s grace period and then escalates to SIGKILL,
which the kernel delivers without the process cooperating. Safe here: the
target is verified to be our own listener, it holds no user data, and its
pidfile is cleaned up by the caller.

* fix(hotkey): stable process identity and UNKNOWN-safe upgrade handoff (YAO-341)

Closes the two remaining blocking review items on PR #31.

- Version drift with unverifiable ownership spawned a duplicate. When the
  recorded version was stale AND `ps` could not classify the pidfile's owner,
  `_retire_superseded_listener()` returned None ("nothing to retire"), so the
  caller deleted the artifacts and started a second listener while the first
  was still running and holding its EventTap. Reproduced: spawn=True,
  artifacts deleted, old process alive.

  The three cases are now distinguished. Absent and FOREIGN still permit
  cleanup and spawn — a recycled PID means our listener is gone. Only a live
  process whose ownership is UNKNOWN blocks, returning UNVERIFIABLE so the
  caller changes nothing and retries next session.

  Getting this wrong in the obvious direction is a real risk: my first attempt
  blocked on any live PID, which broke respawn over a FOREIGN pidfile and
  would have stranded users with no listener. A test now pins FOREIGN, absent
  and UNKNOWN separately.

- The escalation trusted a bare integer PID. Ownership was verified once, then
  SIGTERM, a grace period, and SIGKILL all targeted that integer. If the
  listener exited on SIGTERM and the kernel recycled its number during the
  wait, `_process_alive()` reported the bystander as alive and the escalation
  sent SIGKILL to it.

  `coord.process_identity()` now pairs the PID with its start time, giving a
  handle that a recycled PID cannot forge. `get_listener_target()` returns
  `(pid, identity)`, and every non-zero signal — including the poll loop and
  the SIGKILL escalation — re-confirms the same identity is still OWNED. A
  changed or missing identity means the process we wanted gone is gone, so the
  handoff reports success rather than escalating.

Adds 12 tests: version drift crossed with `ps` OSError / SubprocessError /
TimeoutExpired asserting zero signal, zero cleanup, zero spawn and the live
process untouched; FOREIGN and absent PIDs still spawning; identity shape,
uniqueness and unavailability; and the race itself — PID recycled after
SIGTERM asserts no SIGKILL, plus identity changing before the first signal
asserts no signal at all.
